text:
maya: Quick check — I sketched an ownership handoff matrix for the modularization sprint. Want feedback before I put it in the repo.

sam: Nice. Is this the thing that maps service boundaries -> SLA tiers -> oncall owners?

maya: Yup exactly. Also maps data ownership, rollout fallbacks, and rollback owners. Trying to avoid surprises during the strangler cutover.

rachel: Can you paste the matrix here? A tiny sample would help.

maya: sure — quick snippet:```
service      | owner_team | sla_tier | rollback_owner | fallback_model
request-router | infra-team | gold     | infra-oncall   | router-lite
session-mesh   | runtime     | silver   | runtime-oncall  | session-proxy
kv-cache       | eng-platform| bronze   | platform-oncall | cache-readonly
```

jordan: That's helpful. Two thoughts: 1) we need a clear definition for each SLA tier (p95 latency, availability, recovery window). 2) Rollback_owner shouldn't be the same as owner_team in all cases — we want a separate fallback ops lead.

maya: Agreed. I put a draft SLA rubric in the doc: gold = p95 < 50ms, availability >= 99.95%, RTO < 5m. Silver = p95 < 150ms, availability >= 99.9%, RTO < 15m. Bronze = best-effort. Thoughts?

sam: Those numbers look reasonable for the hotpath pieces. For enrichment/background workers we should probably cap bronze to p95 < 500ms.

rachel: Also call out cost constraints — dedicated infra for gold only. Bronze should be able to live on shared low-priority queues.

maya: Good call. I'll add a column for "preferred infra class" and a short note about cost guardrails.

ops-bot: Reminder: please link the matrix to the runbook under docs/operational/ownership-matrix.md by EOW.

jordan: On the handoff process — propose 3 phases: align owners + SLAs, run cross-team canary for 2 weeks, then cut traffic 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated fallback after each step. Anyone opposed?

sam: No objection. Add an instrumentation gate at each step: latency regressions, error budget burn, and memory spike detection.

maya: I'll bake those gates into the rollout playbook. Also want to include a tech-debt paydown column that captures "tolerable debt" vs "blocking debt" for each service. That way we can prioritize which services must be cleaned before cutover.

rachel: Can you give an example of blocking debt?

maya: Sure — anything that prevents safe rollback or causes cross-tenant data leakage. For example, shared in-process caches that don't respect tenant context — blocking. Minor logging noise — tolerable.

jordan: We should also capture compatibility contracts (API versions + migration window). If an old consumer can't be migrated in the 30d window, escalate to product.

sam: Who's going to own filling the matrix? Feels like a lot for one person.

maya: I'll start the first pass and assign owners for each row. Ask teams to review + sign off within 5 business days. I'll ping each lead.

rachel: Suggestion — add a "testing checklist" column: perf smoke, chaos network, schema backward-compatibility, canary traffic. Makes reviews faster.

maya: Excellent. Will add. Action items: 1) maya: publish first-pass matrix to docs + PR by tomorrow. 2) team leads: review & sign off within 5 days. 3) eng-sre: define rollout gates + automation hooks. 4) product: confirm migration windows for external integrators.

ops-bot: Action logged: matrix_published -> pending reviews.

sam: If anyone wants to pair on the SRE hooks, ping me. I can help draft the Prometheus rules + alert templates.

jordan: One last ask — can we include a short rollback runbook per service (1-2 bullet steps) so oncall isn't flipping through a long doc during an incident?

maya: Yes — will add a condensed rollback snippet for each service in the matrix row.

rachel: This is shaping up. Thanks maya.

maya: thanks all — will post the PR link when ready.

sam: :thumbsup:
